verdict.reasoning: Patient describes “really bad tummy egg… at the bottom… lower abdomen… in the middle… below [belly button]”, present “a few days ago… really getting worse with time”, “there all the time”, and rates pain “Maybe 8”/10.

She reports “vaginal, sometime bleeding, but it's like light color” after her period ended (“my period stopped like last two weeks ago… this is different… light pink color”). She also states periods are “sporadic. Like not the time it changes” while using Implanon.
Patient: “I feel nausea. Like, I feel like vomiting, but I don't. I get nauseated, but I don't vomit.”
She had constipation last week: “I was constipated for a week…”, and now: “this week it seems to be… okay. It's fine now… I’m going to the toilet every day.”

She says last period was “about two weeks. Three weeks ago” and confirms it was normal: “And was your last period normal? Patient: Yeah.” She also notes ongoing light bleeding since it stopped: “my period stopped like last two weeks ago. And this is different… light pink color.”

She answers yes to regular intercourse and recent sex: “Are you having sexual intercourse regularly? Patient: Yes… I just had [4 days ago].” She states contraceptive use: “I use it from last one year. Plan on calling. Plan.” and later confirms “your Implanon was just put in a year ago? Patient: Yes.”

Transcript confirms a pregnancy test “around like a month ago” and that it was before current pain, but the result (negative) is never stated. The doctor advises a pregnancy test today, but that is part of plan, not the historical HPI. Therefore stating it was negative is added information.

She denies fever, dyspnea, and orthostatic symptoms: “Any difficulty breathing…? Patient: No.” “Do you feel feverish? Patient: No.” “Do you feel faint when you stand up? Patient: No.” However, for urinary frequency she says the opposite: “I don't really go often like before. So, yeah,” indicating decreased frequency, not denying changes.

She denies other vaginal discharge: “There is no extra other vaginal discharge. Just [the light bleeding].” But when asked about “weight loss or blood in the stool or urine?” she answers, “Yes, I have. As I said, I have some… discharge and bleeding…”, which is ambiguous but not a clear denial of weight loss. The statement that she denies weight loss is not supported and conflicts with her initial ‘Yes’ response.
She reports an allergy: “Yeah, I have allergy. I have Amy… Ammo. Excellent allergy.” (unclear type but clearly an allergy).
Surgical history: “Anything else? Have you had any operations? Patient: No.”
Obstetric history: “Have you had any pregnancies? Patient: No.”
She explicitly reports an allergy: “Yeah, I have allergy. I have Amy… Ammo. Excellent allergy.”
Occupation: “And what's your job day to day? Patient: Yeah, I'm a teacher.”
Living situation: “And who do you live with at home? Patient: My husband and my husband's family.”
Substance use: “And do you smoke or drink alcohol? You take any other drugs? Patient: No.”
Travel: “Have you been abroad recently? Patient: Yes… About a year… Oh, a year ago. Not recently? No.” This supports last travel about a year ago and none recently.
The transcript contains no vital signs or physical exam findings; the doctor only discusses arranging a future examination and does not document any current exam.

The transcript does not state an assessment or differential such as ‘gynecological etiology, Implanon-related spotting, early pregnancy, or pelvic pathology.’ The doctor only notes pain, need for exam, and pregnancy testing without explicit differential diagnoses.
Constipation course is noted: last week constipation, now resolved: “I was constipated for a week… this week it seems to be… okay. It's fine now.”
Nausea without vomiting is part of the problem list: “I feel nausea… I get nauseated, but I don't vomit.” It is clearly recognized in the history and relevant to assessment.

Plan for in-person exam: “we can arrange a face to face examination where they can see you in a clinic and do an abdominal examination and advise further…” This implies abdominal and pelvic/gynecologic evaluation given vaginal bleeding, though ‘pelvic’ is not said explicitly; arranging a face-to-face abdominal exam is clearly supported.
Pregnancy test plan: “The other thing we would need to do is to do a pregnancy test today if possible. So if you can do that today and if it's positive, we need to see you straight away.”

Safety-netting: “In the meantime, if it gets a lot worse or you. You're not holding any fluids down, then we should see you before then.” This matches instructions to seek earlier care if pain worsens or she cannot tolerate fluids.
Support line for appointment: “Would you be happy to call the support line and arrange that appointment?… if you call the support line and make an appointment, we'll go from there.”
